spans.s:
Bhaya-da Āsamātya (‘descendant of Asamāti’) is the name of a king in the Jaiminīya upaniṣad brāhmaṇa. Oertel, however, seems to take the name as Abhayada, but this is not probable, for Bhayada is a name in the Purāṇas.
Foot notes iv. 8, 7.
Journal of the American Oriental Society, 16, 247.

Bhayamāna is, according to Sāyaṇa, the name of a man in one hymn of the Rigveda, which is ascribed by the Anukramaṇī (Index) to his authorship. The interpretation is, however, uncertain.
Foot notes i. 100, 17. Cf. Muir, Sanskrit Texts, 12, 266.

Bhāya-jātya, ‘descendant of Bhayajāta,’ is the patronymic of Nikothaka in the vaṃśa brāhmaṇa.
Foot notes Indische Studien, 4, 373; Max Müller, Ancient Sanskrit Literature, 444.
